faq.q: What does the flush valve do?
faq.a: The flush valve is a seal at the bottom of the cistern. Pressing the flush lifts it, so the stored water drops into the bowl all at once.
asks: What happens inside the tank when I flush?

faq.q: Why does a toilet flush so strongly?
faq.a: Because the bowl fills so fast that the curved pipe behind it fills completely and starts a siphon. The falling water pulls the bowl contents after it until air gets in.
asks: How does a toilet siphon work?
Why does the water get sucked away?

faq.q: Why does a toilet gurgle at the end of a flush?
faq.a: The gurgle is air rushing into the bent pipe as the bowl empties. The air breaks the siphon, which stops the pull and lets the bowl refill.
asks: What is the gurgling noise after flushing?

faq.q: Where does the water go when you flush?
faq.a: It flows down the soil pipe into the drain and then the sewer, which carries it by gravity to a treatment works where it is cleaned.

faq.q: Why do toilets have two flush buttons?
faq.a: A dual flush uses a small flush, about 3 or 4 litres, for liquid waste and a full one, about 6 litres, for solids. That saves a lot of water over a year.

facts: Most modern toilets use a siphon in the bent pipe behind the bowl to empty it quickly.
Alexander Cumming patented the S-shaped trap for flush toilets in 1775.
Dual-flush toilets typically offer a full flush of about 6 litres and a reduced flush of about 3 to 4 litres.

wrong.1: The water is not there to cool anything.
